smoke.notes: Reason: CF worker requires deploy — scripts/deploy.sh authenticates to the Cloudflare REST API (token verify, KV namespace, script upload, cron schedules) and the judge relay further calls DeepInfra; lane rules forbid network/deploy. Honest offline dog-food DID run instead: node scripts/validate-dialect.mjs (stdlib-only, deterministic, no network) → 38/38 checks PASS, exit 0; fixture bytes sha256 6abf46592d775995e4645e8198fe6d21f53deeb704fa99b55f23497379d832ad; organ content address 677a3c79…; VERDICT: BOTH implementations (worker validators + toolkit primitives) validate the canonical fixture and reject the negative controls. Note: the repo carries no wrangler.toml — deployment config lives entirely in scripts/deploy.sh via the REST API.

essence: Three Cloudflare workers: content-addressed organ store, independent drift watcher, judge relay.

ideas.name: content-addressed organ store
ideas.statement: The loader derives organ id = sha256hex(canonicalJSON(manifest)) SERVER-SIDE (the client cannot choose an id), serves immutable responses (ETag = id, Cache-Control immutable), treats identical re-upload as idempotent rather than conflict, and re-derives every commitment before declaring a stored organ bootable (src/organ-boot-loader/worker.js:8-11, 516-566, 594+).

ideas.name: dialect unification (L15)
ideas.statement: One registered schema string quilt.organ.manifest/v1 (schema/organ-manifest.v1.json) whose manifest body is the toolkit's law verbatim plus the registered whole-state commitment; legacy quilt.organ.v1 stays accepted with a x-quilt-schema-deprecated header during transition; /verify always reports which dialect a stored organ was served as; one shared fixture is validated by BOTH implementations through the exact production code paths (worker header comment :18-28, :49-51; scripts/validate-dialect.mjs).

ideas.name: the watcher shares no code path with the watched
ideas.statement: organ-watcher (cron 0 * * * *, forceable via POST /check) independently re-derives every commitment from stored bytes — manifest digest == id, stateHash, receipt chain under the organ's own dialect law — because calling the loader's /verify from the same account is platform-blocked (same-account worker→worker fetch on *.workers.dev gets error-1042-class 404, receipted in receipts/ORGAN-WATCHER.md); drift findings are recorded and never deleted (src/organ-watcher/worker.js:7-31).

ideas.name: score-first judge relay
ideas.statement: judge-relay fans a candidate out to up to 8 judge models on DeepInfra's OpenAI-compatible endpoint under a fixed scoring contract (verdict's FIRST line must be 'SCORE: <n>/10' so tiny token budgets still parse), returns raw verdict text beside parsed scores, and aggregates mean/min/max/spread (src/judge-relay/worker.js:23-26, 48-51, 212-226).

parts.name: canonical() fail-closed canonicalizer
parts.essence: The registered law, identical to the toolkit's canonicalJson on every JSON-representable value (proven by the cross-canonicalizer battery); throws at the exact path for undefined, non-finite numbers, bigint, function, symbol.
parts.gate: values with no stable JSON meaning throw (fail-closed) instead of coercing
parts.failure_mode: TypeError canonical: undefined/NaN/bigint/function/symbol at <path> (throws, not a named code)

parts.name: sha256hex over WebCrypto
parts.essence: crypto.subtle.digest → lowercase hex; the single hashing primitive every commitment re-derivation uses.

parts.name: shared KV namespace substrate
parts.essence: One KV namespace 'quilt-organ-store' holds organ:{id} envelope bytes and meta:{id} rows for the loader, plus watch:{id} rows and watch:_lastRun for the watcher — two services, one substrate, writes partitioned by key prefix; the watcher never deletes anything.
parts.gate: watcher writes only watch:* rows; loader writes only organ:/meta: rows

parts.name: canonical receipt chain check
parts.essence: receipts[i] = {seq, op (object, non-empty type), prev, hash}, hash = sha256(canon({seq,op,prev})), GENESIS-anchored at receiptRange.start, full window (length == count) — every digest recomputed server-side, not just linkage.
parts.gate: full window present; every hash re-derives
parts.failure_mode: RECEIPT_INVALID (reasons: hash mismatch, prev does not link, seq discontinuity, op not an object)

parts.name: legacy receipt chain check
parts.essence: The worker-original law kept unchanged for transition: receipts[i].digest = sha256(canon({seq,op,cell,prev,payload})), receipts[0].prev = 'genesis', count == receiptRange.length, each digest in manifest.receiptRange.
parts.gate: every legacy digest re-derives and matches the range

parts.name: validateCanonicalBundle
parts.essence: Full canonical-dialect validation — the toolkit's validateManifest + verifyChain + computeManifestHash law PLUS the registered whole-state commitment: manifestHash self-cover, stateHash over whole state, cellsSha256 over the cells map, per-cell stateHashes, receiptRange {start,end,count} consistency, genesis anchoring; returns {ok, errors:[{code, detail}]} — exported so the harness runs the EXACT production code.
parts.gate: all three commitment levels (manifest, whole state, per-cell) must re-derive
parts.failure_mode: MANIFEST_INVALID | MANIFESTHASH_MISMATCH | STATEHASH_MISMATCH | STATE_INVALID | CELLSSHA256_MISMATCH | CELL_STATE_MISSING | CELL_STATEHASH_MISMATCH | RECEIPT_INVALID

parts.name: idempotent envelope store
parts.essence: Content-addressing makes identical re-upload idempotent, not a conflict: existing organ:{id} → refresh meta:{id} and return stored:false, alreadyExisted:true; new bundle → 201 with etag and verify path.
parts.gate: same bytes → same id → no duplicate objects

parts.name: server-side id derivation
parts.essence: The organ id is re-derived from the manifest bytes at PUT time — a client cannot choose, claim, or squat an id; the store's address space is owned by the canonical form of the content.
parts.gate: id is always sha256hex(canonical(manifest)) computed by the worker

parts.name: dialect admission + deprecation policy
parts.essence: detectDialect routes canonical (bundle.schema) vs legacy (bundle.schemaVersion) vs refuse; legacy is accepted during transition but every legacy response carries x-quilt-schema-deprecated plus a deprecation note pointing at the registered schema doc; unsupported dialect → 400 naming both expected strings.
parts.gate: only the two registered dialect strings pass; legacy is loudly deprecated, never silent

parts.name: token auth by digest compare
parts.essence: Authorization: Bearer or x-quilt-token against WORKER_UPLOAD_TOKEN, compared as sha256 digests (length-independent), never logged or reflected; shared fleet single-token discipline across loader, watcher, and judge relay.
parts.gate: no token, or missing binding → refuse

parts.name: body budget guard
parts.essence: 8 MiB guard on declared content-length and actual text length (KV value limit is 25 MiB; boots stay lean) — checked before parse and before validation.
parts.gate: declared and actual size both ≤ MAX_BODY_BYTES

parts.name: watcher drift tri-state policy
parts.essence: driftDetected is strictly three-valued: true (re-derivation failed — a FINDING, receipted, never deleted), false (every commitment re-derives), null (indeterminate: dialect unknown, or re-derivation threw, or meta row exists without organ bytes — which is itself counted as drift); MAX_ORGANS 512 hard stop for free-tier discipline.
parts.gate: a stored organ that fails re-derivation is never silently dropped nor auto-deleted
parts.failure_mode: 'stored envelope missing or unreadable (meta row without organ bytes)' → driftDetected:true

parts.name: loader HTTP routes
parts.essence: GET / (service index with dialect + endpoint map), GET /organs (list with schemaVersion + cell/receipt counts), GET /organ/{sha256} (ETag + immutable cache + dialect headers), GET /organ/{sha256}/verify, PUT /organ (auth + validate + store); HEAD allowed on organ reads; OPTIONS preflight.
parts.gate: route table matches the advertised index exactly

parts.name: watcher check cycle + status dashboard
parts.essence: runCycle lists every meta:* id (paged, capped), re-derives each organ, writes watch rows + _lastRun {ranAt, trigger, durationMs, organsTracked, bootable, drifted, indeterminate}; GET /status serves every last check plus a fleetHealth summary; POST /check forces a cycle under auth; cron 0 * * * *.
parts.gate: one record per organ per cycle; summary counts must add up

parts.name: judge relay fan-out
parts.essence: POST /judge validates candidate/rubric/judges (≤8, candidate ≤256 KiB), fans out concurrently with per-judge timeout (60s), model alias resolution, Qwen-family thinking disabled by default, per-judge verdicts {ok, score, content, reasoning_head, usage, latency_ms, error?} plus aggregate {mean, min, max, spread, n, n_total}.
parts.gate: judges ≤ 8; candidate ≤ 256 KiB; unsupported provider refuses per-judge without failing the batch

parts.name: score-first parsing contract
parts.essence: The fixed SCORING_CONTRACT instruction forces 'SCORE: <n>/10' as the verdict's first line; parseScore tolerantly finds the line, clamps to [0,10], and reports hasContractLine separately — raw verdict text always rides beside the parsed score so a parse miss is visible, not lossy.
parts.gate: score must come from the contract line; clamp at [0,10]
parts.failure_mode: score:null with hasContractLine:true (contract violated) — visible in the response, never fabricated

parts.name: /verify boot-readiness report
parts.essence: GET /organ/{id}/verify recomputes everything server-side, trusting nothing on arrival: checks {manifestDigestMatchesId, stateHashMatchesState, receiptChain, manifestHashSelfCover, cellsSha256MatchesState, perCellStateHashes} → {bootable, reason, dialect} — the check-before-boot instrument any agent can call.
parts.gate: bootable only if every commitment re-derives
parts.failure_mode: bootable:false with the failing check named in the map

parts.name: watcher independence + platform-block receipt
parts.essence: The monitor shares NO code path with the service it watches; the cheaper alternative (calling the loader's /verify over HTTP) was live-tested first and is platform-blocked (same-account worker→worker fetch on *.workers.dev → instant error-1042-class unparseable 404, ~2 ms), receipted in receipts/ORGAN-WATCHER.md — re-derivation is the sanctioned fallback and strictly stronger for drift monitoring.
parts.gate: zero shared validation code with the loader

parts.name: shared-fixture dual-implementation harness
parts.essence: scripts/validate-dialect.mjs proves BOTH organ implementations validate the same canonical fixture and reject every negative control, including a cross-canonicalizer battery (byte-equality on JSON edge cases + deterministic pseudo-random corpus) and fail-closed parity (undefined/NaN/Infinity/bigint throw in BOTH); exit 0 iff every check holds; deterministic, no network.
parts.failure_mode: exit 1 fail-closed on any disagreement between implementations
parts.evidence: scripts/validate-dialect.mjs:1-60; run this lane: 38/38 PASS, fixture sha256 6abf4659…

parts.name: secret custody discipline
parts.essence: All credentials come from a gitignored .env.keys; secrets attach as Worker secret_text bindings at upload; metadata JSON written to a chmod-600 temp file and removed after; the script contains none of them — the same discipline the fleet applies to push tokens.
parts.gate: no credential ever enters the repo or the uploaded metadata file's leftovers

cells.expr: manifest law + 3 commitment levels + receipt chain → {ok, errors[]}
full window; hash re-derivation per receipt
KV organ:{id} + meta:{id}; idempotent on existing id
list meta:*, independently re-derive each, write watch:{id} + _lastRun (tri-state drift)
GET /status → every last check + fleetHealth summary
match 'SCORE: n/10' (first line preferred), clamp [0,10], report hasContractLine
Promise.all over ≤8 judges → DeepInfra chat/completions + aggregate spread
run worker exports + toolkit primitives over one fixture + negative controls; exit 0 iff all pass

layer_logic.0: KV namespace + canonical JSON + WebCrypto sha256 — the substrate is one key-partitioned store whose only addressing authority is the canonical form of the content.
layer_logic.1: Validation pipelines re-derive every commitment from bytes (three commitment levels: manifest self-cover, whole-state, per-cell; plus per-dialect receipt chains) — nothing is trusted on arrival, in either implementation.
layer_logic.2: Policy: token auth by digest compare, 8 MiB budget, dialect admission with loud deprecation, server-side id derivation, watcher tri-state drift (finding / boot-ready / indeterminate) with a never-delete rule and a free-tier cap.
layer_logic.3: Interface: the loader's PUT/GET/verify route table with immutable caching and CORS-open reads, the watcher's cron + /check + /status, the relay's POST /judge fan-out with a score-first parsing contract.
layer_logic.4: Evidence: /verify's named check map, /status's fleet health summary, dialect + deprecation headers on every response, the platform-block receipt justifying watcher independence, and the 38-check shared-fixture harness that ran green offline this lane.
